(By Smt. Aruna V., Adv.)
 Judgment
The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries and damages sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 02-11-2023.

2. The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 02-11-2023 at about 8.10 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding by riding motor bike bearing No. KA-52-L- 7176 on T Beguru - Thyamagondalu road, Gundenahalli cross, near Hanumanthegowdana palya road, at that time the driver of the Car bearing No.KA-05-AB-8072 came from Thyamagondalu road in opposite direction, at very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor bike of the petitioner and caused the accident.
Due to the impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, petitioner was shifted to Government hospital,
Thymagondalu, wherein he took first aid treatment and then he was shifted to Hemavathi Orthopedic & Trauma Centre, Tumkur wherein petitioner took treatment as an inpatient, he was diagnosed communited fracture shaft right leg and also underwent surgery.
Prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy and was working as a Assistant Village Accountant and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.

Due to the accidental injuries,
petitioner is not able to do his work as earlier and suffering from permanent disability and lost his earning capacity.

The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending Car are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.15,00,000/-
with interest.

3. Inspite of service of notice, respondent No.1 owner has not appeared before the court, hence,
placed as Exparte.
After service of summons, Respondent No.2 - insurance company has appeared through its counsel and filed written statement by contending that, the complaint was filed after delay of one day.
Further it has admitted the issuance of policy to the offending Car bearing No.KA-05-AB-8072.

It has contended that there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the offending Car bearing No.KA-05-AB-8072 and the accident caused due to the negligence of the petitioner himself who Sathishkumar T R vs Rajashekar R on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10854904/

sentences.text: Further contended that, the offending Car had no permit at the time of accident.
Further it has also denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner, involvement of the offending car in the alleged accident.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive, exorbitant, arbitrary and disproportionate.
Hence, this respondent prays to dismiss the petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent driving of Toyota Innova Car bearing No.KA-05-AB-8072 by its driver, in RTA took place on 02-11-2023 at about 8.10 p.m., on T- Beguru - Thy- magondalu road, Gundenahalli cross, Hanumanthe gowdanapalya road, Bengaluru ?
2. Whether the petitioner is enti- tled for compensation?
If so, what amount and from whom?
3 . What Order or Award?
5. In order to prove the claim petition, the petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to 14.
Further Dr.Nagaraj B.N. Orthopedics Surgeon is examined as PW.2 and MRO of Hemavathi hospital is examined as PW.3 and got marked the documents at Ex.P15 to 19.
On the other hand, the respondent No.1 examined FDA at RTO, Nelamangala as RW1 and got marked 3 documents at Ex.R.1 to R.3.
further the respondent No.1 examined its official as RW2 and got marked 2 documents at Ex.R.4 & R.5.

6. Heard the arguments and perused the materials and evidence that are available on record.
7.
My findings on the above issues are as under.

Issue No.1 : In the affirmative;
 Issue No.2 : In the affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final orders  for the following:-

 ISSUE NO.1 :
8. That by reiterating all the averments made in the petition, the petitioner has filed his affidavit in lieu of- examination in-chief, which is considered as PW.1.

In support of his case, he has produced certified copies of FIR, complaint, spot mahazar along with sketch, IMV notice and reply, IMV report, wound certificate, charge sheet which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 9.

sentences.text: On perusal of Ex.P1 - FIR which is registered on the basis of Ex.P2 first information given by the petitioner himself by alleging the rash and negligent driving by the driver of Car bearing No.KA-05-AB-8072.
The contents of Ex.P.1 & 2 are in consonance with the petition averments.
After the registration of FIR, the IO has conducted spot mahazar and sketch as per Ex.P3 & P4.

On perusal of spot mahazar at Ex.P3 the accident spot is in the left side edge of the road wherein it is found that the offending Car bearing No.KA-05-AB-8072 came to its wrong side and dashed against the motorcycle of the petitioner and also an another car.

10. Further Ex.P.7 is the IMV report wherein it is found that the petitioner's motor cycle bearing No.
KA.05-AB-8072 has got damages in its front bumper right side, right side head light assembly,
Bonnet right side, right side front fender and in the same way the offending Car bearing No.KA-05-AB-8072 has got damages in its head light assembly, handle bar left side damaged, front wheel mudguard, front fork, front botgh side indicator, clutch lever, rear both side indicator damaged.
The contents of Ex.P3, P4 & P7 helped the petitioner to prove the negligence of the driver of Car bearing No.KA-05-AB-8072 in the alleged accident.
The driver of the offending Car bearing No.KA-05-AB-8072 came to his extreme righht side and caused the accident by his negligence.

11. The learned counsel for the respondent No.1 insurer vehemently argues that there is an inordinate delay of 1 day in lodging the FIR and the same cannot be brushed aside lightly, instead has to be construed as a circumstance showing that the case is an afterthought and the offending vehicle is implicated in the case even though it is not involved in the accident.
But not every delay would move this court to view the case of the petitioner doubtfully.
Because there might be genuine circumstances that could have contributed to the delay.
In fact only if the delay is left unexplained the same needs to be viewed seriously.

12. No doubt in the facts of this case, the accident occurred on 02-11-2023 at about 8.10 p.m. but the FIR was lodged on 03-11-2023 and hence it is evident that the FIR is lodged after one day of occurrence of the accident.

But the petitioner in the Ex.P2 first information it is stated that soon after the accident he was shifted to Government hospital, Thymagondalu and thereafter shifted to Hemavathi hospital and underwent with treatment, hence, they were unable to give the complaint immediately.

The accident was at 8.30 p.m, i.e., in the night and the FIR was registered on the next day morning and also the FIR was registered on the basis of the statement given by the petitioner in Tumkur District Hospital in the presence of doctors.
Hence the delay of one day, in the light of reasons assigned by the PW.1 and also as mentioned in the Ex.P2, complaint it cannot be considered as inordinate.

13. Ex.P9 is the charge sheet also came to be filed on the driver of the offending Car bearing No.KA-05-AB- 8072 for the offences punishable U/Sec.279 and 338 of IPC and Sec.187, 56 of MV Act wherein, the IO has opined that the negligence is on the part of driver of Car bearing No.KA-05-AB-8072.
By producing these documents, the petitioner prima-facie established the occurrence of accident and also the alleged negligence of the driver of the Car bearing No.KA-05-AB-8072.

The view taken by this Court that the police records are prima- facie proof in support of the case of the petitioner, is supported by the decision rendered in Kishan Gopal and another Vs. 15.

It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the inc ident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.

Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

where the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka considering the fact that the rider of the offending vehicle was not examined to prove any contributory negligence on the part of scooterist held that the accident had occurred due to rash or negligent driving by the rider of the offending van.

sentences.text: In view of the ratio laid down in the authorities referred to above and applying the settled principle of law to the case at hand, which is further supported by the oral and documentary evidence adduced by PW-1, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident leading to this case indeed occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of Car bearing No.KA- 05-AB-8072 resulting in petitioner sustaining injuries.
During the course of cross examination of petitioner, except a suggestion nothing has been elicited so as to disprove the case of the petitioner.
There are no material evidence to prove that the petitioner's negligence was the reason for the said accident.

Even though the respondent examined its official as RW2, the evidence of RW2 is based on the police documents and RW2 is not an eyewitness, hence, the evidence of RW2 failed to rebut the case of the petitioner in respect of the fact of accident and the negligence of the driver of offending Car bearing No.KA-05-AB-8072.
17.
As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.

All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 02-11-2023 which is caused by the driver of the Car bearing No.KA-05-AB-8072.
There is no reasons to discard the evidence of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Accordingly, issue No.1 answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:
18.
As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that he has sustained injuries in RTA which is caused by the respondent No.1.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.
19. The petitioner has produced wound certificate as per Ex.P8 which shows that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
Further, the petitioner has also produced discharge summary as per Ex.P10.

On perusal of the same it shows that, petitioner took treatment as an inpatient at Hemavathi hospital from 04-11-2023 to 07-11-2023 for a period of 4 days and sustained comminuted fracture of shaft right leg and also underwent operation for CRIF with IMIL for right leg under SA done on 04.11.2023.
The petitioner examined one Dr.Nagaraj B.N., who assessed the disability.

As per the evidence of PW.2 doctor the petitioner has sustained injury to comminuted fracture of shaft right leg who has also produced the clinical notes and X-ray which reveals that the petitioner has sustained the permanent physical disability of right lower limb at 42% and to the whole body at 14%.
20. According to the petitioner he was working as a Assistant Village Accountant and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.
To prove his avocation and income, he has not produced any documents.

21. While determining the compensation this court has to look into the pain and sufferings, medical expenses, diet, food, nourishment, attendant and conveyance charges and loss of amenities and enjoyment of life that the PW-1 has suffered, which are discussed herein below:

sentences.text: The petitioner has relied upon Ex.P.8 & P10 - wound certificate and discharge summary, which make it crystal clear that PW-1 has sustained grievous injury.
The petitioner was admitted to Hemavathi hospital from 04-11-2023 to 07-11-2023 for a period of 4 days.

Hence keeping in mind the injuries mentioned in wound certificate and discharge summary, it can be said that the petitioner must have undergone some amount of physical pain and sufferings, for which, an amount of Rs.60,000/- can be held to be just and proper compensation under this head.
(B) TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner has produced the medical bills marked at Ex.P11 amounting to Rs.49,020/-.
These bills are not disputed by the respondents and no grounds are made out to disbelieve these bills.
Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case in combined with the alleged injuries the petitioner is entitle for the reimbursement of the same by rounding of the same i.e., Rs.49,100/-.
(C) TOWARDS DIET, FOOD, NOURISHMENT:
As already observed the Ex.P-8 & 10, makes it amply clear that the petitioner underwent treatment for the injuries sustained by him.
During the said period the petitioner might have taken assistance from others and taken diet food.
On consideration of the injuries sustained by the petitioner this Tribunal is of the opinion that it is just and proper to award an amount of Rs.20,000/- under this head.
c) Loss of income during laid up period:
The petitioner has stated that he was working as Village accountant and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
To prove the said fact the petitioner has not produced any document.

In the absence of any document the notional income of the petitioner is considered at Rs.16,000/-
p.m. as the accident is of the year 2023.
As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P10 petitioner was admitted to Hemavathi Hospital and underwent the operation.

Thereafter usually the healing period has to be considered for which in the absence of evidence, this court is of the opinion that in total four months period may be considered under this head as a loss of income.
So, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.16,000 X 4 months = Rs.64,000/- during the laid up period.

d) Disability;- To prove the nature of injuries sustained by him the petitioner examined Dr.
Kantharaju, Orthopedic Surgeon as PW.2, through him OPD book and X-ray are marked at Ex.P16 & P17.

According to the evidence of this witness the petitioner sustained undisplaced fracture of right medial malleoli, head of 2nd metacarpal undisplaced fracture, undisplaced avulsion fracture of left medial malleoli, right tibial condyle avulsion fracture, left proximal fibula head fracture.

Hence, I inclined to award future loss of income at Rs.16,000/- X 12 X 17 X 12 % =Rs.3,91,680/- which is the total loss of future income.

g) Towards loss of amenities and enjoyment of life:
The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by him, which might certainly have deprived him of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award a reasonable sum of Rs.30,000/- under this head.
h) Towards future medical expenses:
PW.2 stated that the petitioner needs one more surgery for removal of implants which may cost around Rs.60,000/-.

23. Liability:- The respondent No.1 is the insurer of the Innova Car bearing No. KA-05-AB-8072 and the respondent No.2 is the owner of the said car.
The respondent No.1 in its objection statement has admitted the issuance of policy to the Innova Car bearing No. KA- 05-AB-8072 and the policy was in force at the time of accident.

24. The respondent No.1 examined RW.1 the official of RTO department who produced Ex.R2 'B'
register Extract and Ex.R3 Permit extract.

By producing the said documents, the respondent No.2 insurance company contended that as on the date of accident i.e., on 02-11-2023 there was no valid permit for the offending vehicle bearing No. KA-05-AB-8072 as such it cannot indemnify the liability of respondent No.2.
In this regard, the official i.e., RW.1 cross-examined by the learned counsel for the petitioner.
If we perused the Ex.R1 the permit for the offending vehicle was valid from 30.06.2018 to 29.06.2023.
As per Ex.R.2 there was permit for the Car bearing No.KA-05-AB-8072 for contract carriage permit from 30.06.2018 to 29.06.2023.
the date of accident is 02.11.2023, thereby it is evident that as on the date of accident there was no valid permit for the offending vehicle.
25. The respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle remained exparte and has not made out any grounds to show that there was a valid permit at the time of accident.

The oral answers of RW.1 is not sufficient to consider that there was a valid permit for the offending vehicle at the time of accident because, the documents produced at Ex.R1 to 3 being the public documents clearly establishes that as on the date of accident, there was no valid permit for the offending Car bearing No.KA-05-AB-8072.
26.

The respondent No.1 insurance company has taken specific defence of non existence of permit to the offending vehicle and also taken steps to prove that, the offending vehicle has no permit at the time of accident.

27. The respondent No.2 insurance company has taken specific defence of non existence of permit to the offending Car bearing No.KA-05-AB-8072 and also taken steps to prove that, the offending vehicle has no permit at the time of accident.

Further in the Ex.P9 charge sheet also Sec. 56 R/w.
Sec. 187 is invoked by alleging the non renewing of the permit to the offending vehicle at the time of accident.

sentences.text: The evidence as per Ex.P9 charge sheet as well as Ex.R1 to 3 clearly set out the aspect regarding non existence of the permit for the Car bearing No.KA-05-AB- 8072 at the time of accident.
The respondent No.1 being the owner also made as accused No.2 in the Ex.P9 charge sheet.
The respondent No.1 is placed exparte and has not adduced any evidence by showing the existence of permit to the offending vehicle.
Hence, the insurance company cannot be fastened with liability.
29. By keeping the arguments canvassed by both the parties in background, there is no dispute that at the time of accident the Car bearing No.KA-05-AB-8072 was covered with insurance.
But the violation of the condition of insurance policy is stands established.

30. The learned counsel for the petitioner relied on the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Judicature at Allahabad in First Appeal No.1780/2024 between ICICI Lombard Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd.,
V/s Smt. Arti Devi & 8 others 26.

ICICI Lombard Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd.,
V/s Smt. Arti Devi & 8 others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This Court also finds that since the contract of insurance is between insurer and the owner and has no concern with the claimants who are in fact victims of the accident, language used in Section 149 (prior to amendment) and Section 150 (after amendment) would show that notwithstanding the fact that the insurer may be entitled to avoid or cancel the policy on account of breach of terms thereof, it shall pay to the person entitled to the benefit of the award.
Therefore, whether Insurance Company cancels or does not cancel an insurance policy, the same has nothing to do with the claimants and they are entitled to get the amount from insurer.

It means that claimants' right to receive compensation from the insurer at the first instance is unaffected by the inter-se rights and liabilities arising out of contract between the insurer and the owner.

Further in the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in 2022 ACJ 2771 between Gohar Mohammed V/s U.P State Road Transportation Corporation & others wherein it is held as follows:
"8. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of the material available on record, it clearly reveals that on the date of accident, the appellant did not have a valid and effective permit to ply the offending vehicle on the route where accident took place.

sentences.text: Having extensively gone through the factfinding exercise, it is categorically recorded by MACT that the appellant was neither able to produce/prove the original permit nor was able to prove the information received under RTI Act.
Even if RTI information is considered by which it is not clear as to when the disputed permit was issued and by whom.

The alleged permit was issued on 28.07.2012, i.e.,
on Saturday and no explanation is on record as to why deposit of fee was asked on the next day i.e. Sunday.

Moreover, assuming that permit was valid as per letter of Transport Authority, but it does not of any help to the appellant since the vehicle was being plied on a route different than specified in permit.

The appellant has failed to give any explanation to refute the observations made by MACT to ply the vehicle on Roorkee bypass to Haridwar via Meerut which did not fall within the route of permit issued by Transport Authority.
The said findings of fact have been affirmed by the High Court by the impugned order.

31. In this case, the respondent No.1 owner of the Car bearing No.KA-05-AB-8072 even after the service of summons has not lead any evidence to show that he has not violated the policy condition willfully.

Thereby the conduct of respondent No.1 -owner allowing the Car bearing No.KA-05-AB-8072 to ply on the road without permit is a breach of policy condition and thereby the insurance company cannot be fastened with liability.
The respondent No.1 being the owner cannot take the benefit of his own wrong.

Hence, the judgment relied by the learned counsel for the petitioner is not applicable to the present case on hand and by relying on the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court the owner is liable to pay compensation.

Under such circumstances, the insurance company cannot be fastened with liability of pay and recover when there is clear breach of rules of IMV Act and liability to pay compensation is on the respondent No.1 owner.
Hence, the respondent No.1 owner is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
The petitioner is entitle for compensation with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
Accordingly, this issue answered in the affirmative.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
But not every delay would move this court to view the case of the petitioner doubtfully.
Because there might be genuine circumstances that could have contributed to the delay.
In fact only if the delay is left unexplained the same needs to be viewed seriously.
Hence the delay of one day, in the light of reasons assigned by the PW.1 and also as mentioned in the Ex.P2, complaint it cannot be considered as inordinate.
By producing these documents, the petitioner prima-facie established the occurrence of accident and also the alleged negligence of the driver of the Car bearing No.KA-05-AB-8072.
Wherefore in the absence of any cogent evidence which could rebut the assertions made by PW-1 on oath supported by Ex.P-9 which is the charge sheet and the documents annexed therewith, this court should not have any impediment to conclude that the said documents prima-facie suffice to hold that accident, occurred due to rash and actionable negligence on the part of the driver of Car bearing No.KA-05-AB-8072.
The registration of FIR and filing of the charge- sheet against respondent Nos.1 & 2 are not in dispute, therefore, the Tribunal should have no option but to accept the entire evidence on record and recorded the finding on the contentious issue Nos.1 and 2 in favour of the appellants''.
(Emphasis supplied by me)
15.
During the course of cross examination of petitioner, except a suggestion nothing has been elicited so as to disprove the case of the petitioner.
There are no material evidence to prove that the petitioner's negligence was the reason for the said accident.
Even though the respondent examined its official as RW2, the evidence of RW2 is based on the police documents and RW2 is not an eyewitness, hence, the evidence of RW2 failed to rebut the case of the petitioner in respect of the fact of accident and the negligence of the driver of offending Car bearing No.KA-05-AB-8072.
17.
As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.
All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 02-11-2023 which is caused by the driver of the Car bearing No.KA-05-AB-8072.
There is no reasons to discard the evidence of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
the date of accident is 02.11.2023, thereby it is evident that as on the date of accident there was no valid permit for the offending vehicle.
25. The respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle remained exparte and has not made out any grounds to show that there was a valid permit at the time of accident.
The oral answers of RW.1 is not sufficient to consider that there was a valid permit for the offending vehicle at the time of accident because, the documents produced at Ex.R1 to 3 being the public documents clearly establishes that as on the date of accident, there was no valid permit for the offending Car bearing No.KA-05-AB-8072.
26.
The respondent No.1 insurance company has taken specific defence of non existence of permit to the offending vehicle and also taken steps to prove that, the offending vehicle has no permit at the time of accident.

Therefore, whether Insurance Company cancels or does not cancel an insurance policy, the same has nothing to do with the claimants and they are entitled to get the amount from insurer.
It means that claimants' right to receive compensation from the insurer at the first instance is unaffected by the inter-se rights and liabilities arising out of contract between the insurer and the owner.
31. In this case, the respondent No.1 owner of the Car bearing No.KA-05-AB-8072 even after the service of summons has not lead any evidence to show that he has not violated the policy condition willfully.
Thereby the conduct of respondent No.1 -owner allowing the Car bearing No.KA-05-AB-8072 to ply on the road without permit is a breach of policy condition and thereby the insurance company cannot be fastened with liability.
The respondent No.1 being the owner cannot take the benefit of his own wrong.
Under such circumstances, the insurance company cannot be fastened with liability of pay and recover when there is clear breach of rules of IMV Act and liability to pay compensation is on the respondent No.1 owner.
